analysis: Examined head_text units of docs/provider/cli-reference.md lines 1223-2122. The file_changes map (range_map_complete=true) shows head changes at 743-747 and 751-769 (update --rollback/--yes/--override-quarantine flag docs, not in these units) and at 1852 and 1859-1860 (the `darkbloom update --rollback [--yes]` usage line and its flag rows). Those lines are documentation only. They describe restoring the retained predecessor and quarantining the installed release. This relates to T-043 (watchdog rollback authority) and T-013 (binary modification). The patch excerpt at 751-769 says rollback goes through the watchdog's journaled rollback under the update lease. It contacts no coordinator and cannot be combined with --coordinator. Line 1864 still says the update path verifies hashes. The docs do not say whether rollback re-verifies the predecessor's signature or hash; that lives in UpdateRollback.swift, which was not supplied. Rollback is operator-initiated, and the operator (ADV-001) already controls the binary per TB-003/T-013. A downgrade to a retained, previously installed signed release does not by itself grant trust: TB-011/T-054 make the coordinator's qualification and revocation authoritative. So no regression is evidenced. Integration should confirm three things in UpdateRollback.swift: the retained predecessor is hash/signature-checked before activation; a revoked or unqualified predecessor still fails coordinator authorization; and quarantine via --override-quarantine cannot bypass the T-047 fan-helper stale-provider handling. Other unchanged content in these units (stop/restart, status, doctor, logs refusal lines, report) shows no change.
